rounds.text: Redington Ltd trades at an attractive valuation with a price-to-earnings ratio of 12.9x [E1] and a rules-based screen scoring 88 out of 100 with high confidence [E60]. The fundamental operating engine is firing with exceptional momentum, evidenced by compounded sales growth of 31% and profit growth of 47% over the trailing twelve months [E17, E21], alongside strong underlying core drivers where Technology Solutions Group (TSG) grew 33% excluding large deals [E80]. Capital efficiency remains stellar, with a return on capital employed of 18.4% and return on equity of 16.9% [E12, E13], comfortably outperforming sector medians [E71]. Furthermore, institutional sponsorship is expanding robustly as foreign institutional holdings increased to 63.42% in September 2026 alongside positive money flow [E41, E43], supported by strong operational execution such as ProConnect achieving all-time high quarterly revenues [E75] and operating leverage where revenue grew 48% while expenses grew only 40% [E76]. Conceded: borrowings increased to Rs 6,364 Cr in September 2026 [E39], and Arena recorded a share of loss of INR 115 crores driven by business transitions and impairments [E85].

Conceded: [E44]. Despite the attractive quantitative screen score, significant fundamental vulnerabilities lurk beneath the surface of Redington Ltd. Most notably, cash conversion stands at a meager 0.18x against reported profit for March 2026, revealing that profits are running far ahead of actual cash generation and signaling potential risks in receivables or accruals [E34]. Compounding this liquidity concern, total borrowings surged to Rs 6,364 Cr in September 2026, marking a massive escalation from Rs 2,842 Cr a year earlier [E39], which drives the EV/EBITDA to 11.34x above the sector benchmark [E11]. Furthermore, operations face acute external headwinds, as management explicitly noted that supply chains are under stress in the Middle East due to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, forcing alternative logistics routes [E86]. Geographically, the Arena business is contracting violently with a 37% year-over-year revenue drop driven by exits from Turkish Lira-denominated operations, resulting in Redington's share of losses hitting Rs 115 crores for the quarter including business transitions and impairment losses [E85, E87]. Finally, algorithmic engine flags confirm that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E65], while historical volatility sits at a high 42.7% alongside a severe worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -80.2% [E52, E53].

Conceded: [E34], [E39], [E85], [E86], [E87]. While the bear highlights liquidity and regional headwinds, these concerns ignore the company's robust underlying growth and institutional confidence. The surge in borrowings is balanced by strong operational performance, as evidenced by 31% TTM sales growth and 47% TTM profit growth [E17, E21]. Management is actively managing the Arena transition to improve long-term health, and the core business remains resilient with large deals exceeding INR 3,800 crores [E79, E84]. Furthermore, the institutional backing is strengthening, with foreign holdings increasing by 6.43 percentage points and positive money flow signals [E41, E43]. The company’s ability to maintain a 16.15% ROCE against a sector benchmark of 6.34% demonstrates superior capital efficiency that outweighs temporary supply chain disruptions [E10]. Finally, the market’s valuation remains disconnected from reality, as the current price implies only 5.5% growth compared to the 16% assumed in the base case [E46].

Conceded: [E17, E21]. However, pointing to TTM sales and profit growth masks severe underlying cash-conversion failures, where operating cash flow against reported profit sits at an alarming 0.18x for March 2026, pointing directly to severe receivables and accruals issues [E34]. Furthermore, the bull’s defense of the soaring borrowings ignores the massive escalation to Rs 6,364 Cr in Sep 2026—more than doubling from Rs 2,842 Cr a year prior—which directly threatens financial stability alongside a thin current ratio of 1.41x [E38, E39]. The reliance on Arena’s restructuring as a mere transition ignores the crushing reality of a INR 115 crore quarterly share of loss and a 37% revenue collapse from the Turkish Lira business exit [E85, E87]. While foreign institutional holdings rose, domestic institutions actually cut their stake by 1.91 percentage points down to 16.01%, showing a clear divergence in institutional confidence [E42]. Finally, external supply chain realities like the closed Strait of Hormuz directly undermine the narrative of smooth operations, forcing reliance on precarious alternate shipping routes [E86].

Conceded: [E34, E85, E87]. Despite those points, the severe cash conversion figure for March 2026 is contextualised by healthy operational generation, with operating cash flow hitting Rs 231 Cr and free cash flow reaching Rs 125 Cr [E35, E36]. While borrowings expanded to Rs 6,364 Cr, the company comfortably maintains a moderate global debt-to-equity ratio of 0.55x to 0.59x alongside an adequate current ratio of 1.41x [E37, E38, E39, E83]. The reduction in Arena's debt from $120 million to $90 million directly demonstrates that local business exits are actively curing legacy exposures rather than creating indefinite structural damage [E84]. Although domestic institutions trimmed their stake slightly, overall foreign ownership climbed to 63.42% and institutional money flow signals POSITIVE MONEY FLOW with a holding increase of 1.10 percentage points [E41, E42, E43]. Finally, the underlying business strength is clearly evidenced by ProConnect achieving all-time high quarterly revenues and group large deals exceeding INR 3,800 crores [E75, E79].

The bull points to operating and free cash flows of Rs 231 Cr and Rs 125 Cr [E35, E36], but ignores the severe warning of a 0.18x cash conversion ratio where profits sit drastically ahead of actual cash collection due to receivables and accruals [E34]. While moderate leverage metrics and debt reduction in Arena are highlighted [E37, E38, E39, E83, E84], the bull glosses over the severe disruption in the Arena segment itself, which suffered a 37% revenue drop from Turkish Lira exits and inflicted a massive INR 115 crore loss featuring impairment charges [E85, E87]. Conceded: [E41, E43] regarding foreign institutional holding increases and positive money flow, but this institutional backing does not negate the acute operational stress caused by Middle East supply chain fractures via the closure of the Strait of Hormuz [E86]. Finally, the cited large deal contributions and ProConnect highs [E75, E79] fail to offset the scanX signal engine warning that earnings growth is actively decelerating alongside inconsistent operating margin trends [E32, E33, E65].
